sanskrit: prakṛṣṭair aśubhair grastān anekaiḥ puruṣādhamān patato narake gaṅgā saṃśritān pretya tārayet
english: Men of the lowest sort, seized by manifold and grievous evils and falling into hell — if they have taken refuge in the Gaṅgā, she will carry them across once they have passed beyond death.

sanskrit: te saṃvibhaktā munibhir nūnaṃ devaiḥ savāsavaiḥ ye 'bhigacchanti satataṃ gaṅgām abhigatāṃ suraiḥ
english: Those who continually resort to the Gaṅgā — to whom the gods themselves resort — surely share fellowship with the sages and with the gods, Vāsava at their head.

sanskrit: vinayācārahīnāś ca aśivāś ca narādhamāḥ te bhavanti śivā vipra ye vai gaṅgāṃ samāśritāḥ
english: Even those basest of men, devoid of discipline and right conduct and inauspicious in nature — O brāhmaṇa, they become auspicious if they take refuge in the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: yathā surāṇām amṛtaṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca yathā svadhā sudhā yathā ca nāgānāṃ tathā gaṅgājalaṃ nṛṇām
english: As nectar is to the gods, as the funerary oblation is to the ancestors, as ambrosia is to the serpents, so is the water of the Gaṅgā to mortals.

sanskrit: upāsate yathā bālā mātaraṃ kṣudhayārditāḥ śreyaskāmās tathā gaṅgām upāsantīha dehinaḥ
english: As children tormented by hunger attend upon their mother, so do embodied beings here, longing for what is highest, attend upon the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: svāyaṃbhuvaṃ yathā sthānaṃ sarveṣāṃ śreṣṭham ucyate snātānāṃ saritāṃ śreṣṭhā gaṅgā tadvad ihocyate
english: As the abode of the Self-born is declared the highest of all stations, so the Gaṅgā is here declared, for those who bathe, the foremost of rivers.

sanskrit: yathopajīvināṃ dhenur devādīnāṃ dharā smṛtā tathopajīvināṃ gaṅgā sarvaprāṇabhṛtām iha
english: As the cow is held the sustainer of those who live by her, and the earth of the gods and the rest, so is the Gaṅgā the sustainer here of all that draws breath and lives by her.

sanskrit: devāḥ somārkasaṃsthāni yathā satrādibhir makhaiḥ amṛtāny upajīvanti tathā gaṅgājalaṃ narāḥ
english: As the gods live upon the nectars that abide in soma and the sun, won through the satra and other sacrifices, so do men live upon the water of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: jāhnavīpulinotthābhiḥ sikatābhiḥ samukṣitaḥ manyate puruṣo ''tmānaṃ diviṣṭham iva śobhitam
english: Sprinkled with the sands that rise from the banks of the Jāhnavī, a man deems himself made radiant, as though dwelling in heaven.

sanskrit: jāhnavītīrasaṃbhūtāṃ mṛdaṃ mūrdhnā bibharti yaḥ bibharti rūpaṃ so 'rkasya tamonāśāt sunirmalam
english: He who bears upon his head the clay born of the Jāhnavī's bank bears a form pure and stainless as the sun's, for it destroys all darkness.

sanskrit: gaṅgormibhir atho digdhaḥ puruṣaṃ pavano yadā spṛśate so 'pi pāpmānaṃ sadya evāpamārjati
english: And when the wind, anointed by the waves of the Gaṅgā, touches a man, it wipes away his sin that very instant.

sanskrit: vyasanair abhitaptasya narasya vinaśiṣyataḥ gaṅgādarśanajā prītir vyasanāny apakarṣati
english: For a man scorched by calamities and on the verge of ruin, the joy born of beholding the Gaṅgā draws those calamities away.

sanskrit: haṃsārāvaiḥ kokaravai ravair anyaiś ca pakṣiṇām paspardha gaṅgā gandharvān pulinaiś ca śiloccayān
english: With the cries of swans, the calls of the cakravāka, and the songs of other birds the Gaṅgā vies with the gandharvas, and with her sandbanks she rivals the mountains.

sanskrit: haṃsādibhiḥ subahubhir vividhaiḥ pakṣibhir vṛtām gaṅgāṃ gokulasaṃbādhāṃ dṛṣṭvā svargo 'pi vismṛtaḥ
english: Beholding the Gaṅgā thronged with swans and a great many varied birds, and crowded with herds of cattle, one forgets even heaven.

sanskrit: na sā prītir diviṣṭhasya sarvakāmān upāśnataḥ abhavad yā parā prītir gaṅgāyāḥ puline nṛṇām
english: Not even for one dwelling in heaven and enjoying every desire is there such joy as the supreme joy of men upon the bank of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: vāṅmanaḥkarmajair grastaḥ pāpair api pumān iha vīkṣya gaṅgāṃ bhavet pūtas tatra me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: Even a man here seized by sins born of word, mind, and deed becomes purified by beholding the Gaṅgā — of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: saptāvarān sapta parān pitṝṃs tebhyaś ca ye pare pumāṃs tārayate gaṅgāṃ vīkṣya spṛṣṭvāvagāhya ca
english: By beholding, touching, and plunging into the Gaṅgā, a man delivers seven generations of ancestors below, seven above, and those still beyond them.

sanskrit: śrutābhilaṣitā dṛṣṭā spṛṣṭā pītāvagāhitā gaṅgā tārayate nṝṇām ubhau vaṃśau viśeṣataḥ
english: Heard of, longed for, seen, touched, drunk, and bathed in, the Gaṅgā carries across both lineages of men in full measure.

sanskrit: darśanāt sparśanāt pānāt tathā gaṅgeti kīrtanāt punāty apuṇyān puruṣāñ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: By the sight of her, the touch of her, the drinking of her, and the mere uttering of the name 'Gaṅgā,' she purifies men of no merit by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: ya icchet saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ śrutam eva ca sa pitṝṃs tarpayed gaṅgām abhigamya surāṃs tathā
english: He who would have his birth, his life, and his learning bear fruit should go to the Gaṅgā and there satisfy the ancestors and the gods.

sanskrit: na sutair na ca vittena karmaṇā na ca tat phalam prāpnuyāt puruṣo 'tyantaṃ gaṅgāṃ prāpya yad āpnuyāt
english: Not by sons, nor by wealth, nor by ritual works could a man ever win that utmost fruit which he attains on reaching the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: jātyandhair iha tulyās te mṛtaiḥ paṅgubhir eva ca samarthā ye na paśyanti gaṅgāṃ puṇyajalāṃ śivām
english: Those who, though able, do not look upon the Gaṅgā with her holy and auspicious waters are here the equals of the blind from birth, of the dead, and of cripples.

sanskrit: bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyajñair maharṣibhir upasthitām devaiḥ sendraiś ca ko gaṅgāṃ nopaseveta mānavaḥ
english: What man would not wait upon the Gaṅgā, attended as she is by the great sages who know past, present, and future, and by the gods with Indra at their head?

sanskrit: vānaprasthair gṛhasthaiś ca yatibhir brahmacāribhiḥ vidyāvadbhiḥ śritāṃ gaṅgāṃ pumān ko nāma nāśrayet
english: What man would fail to take refuge in the Gaṅgā, to whom forest hermits, householders, ascetics, celibate students, and the learned have resorted?

sanskrit: utkrāmadbhiś ca yaḥ prāṇaiḥ prayataḥ śiṣṭasaṃmataḥ cintayen manasā gaṅgāṃ sa gatiṃ paramāṃ labhet
english: He who, self-controlled and honored by the wise, with his life-breaths departing fixes his mind in thought upon the Gaṅgā, attains the supreme goal.

sanskrit: na bhayebhyo bhayaṃ tasya na pāpebhyo na rājataḥ ā dehapatanād gaṅgām upāste yaḥ pumān iha
english: The man here who waits upon the Gaṅgā until his body falls away has no fear of any terrors, nor of sins, nor of the king.

sanskrit: gaganād yāṃ mahāpuṇyāṃ patantīṃ vai maheśvaraḥ dadhāra śirasā devīṃ tām eva divi sevate
english: That most holy goddess whom Maheśvara, as she fell from the sky, upheld upon his head — her very self he honors in heaven.

sanskrit: alaṃkṛtās trayo lokāḥ pathibhir vimalais tribhiḥ yas tu tasyā jalaṃ sevet kṛtakṛtyaḥ pumān bhavet
english: The three worlds are adorned by her three pure courses; and the man who resorts to her water becomes one whose every purpose is fulfilled.

sanskrit: divi jyotir yathādityaḥ pitṝṇāṃ caiva candramāḥ deveśaś ca yathā nṝṇāṃ gaṅgeha saritāṃ tathā
english: As the sun is the light in heaven, and the moon the light of the ancestors, and the lord of the gods supreme among men, so is the Gaṅgā here among rivers.

sanskrit: mātrā pitrā sutair dārair viyuktasya dhanena vā na bhaved dhi tathā duḥkhaṃ yathā gaṅgāviyogajam
english: The grief of one parted from mother, father, sons, wife, or wealth is not so great as the grief born of separation from the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: nāraṇyair neṣṭaviṣayair na sutair na dhanāgamaiḥ tathā prasādo bhavati gaṅgāṃ vīkṣya yathā nṛṇām
english: Not from forests, nor from beloved objects of sense, nor from sons, nor from the gaining of wealth comes such serenity to men as comes from beholding the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: pūrṇam induṃ yathā dṛṣṭvā nṛṇāṃ dṛṣṭiḥ prasīdati gaṅgāṃ tripathagāṃ dṛṣṭvā tathā dṛṣṭiḥ prasīdati
english: As the sight of men grows serene at beholding the full moon, so does their sight grow serene at beholding the Gaṅgā, who flows along three paths.

sanskrit: tadbhāvas tadgatamanās tanniṣṭhas tatparāyaṇaḥ gaṅgāṃ yo 'nugato bhaktyā sa tasyāḥ priyatāṃ vrajet
english: He whose being is in her, whose mind is set upon her, who is established in her and devoted to her, and who follows the Gaṅgā with devotion, comes to be dear to her.

sanskrit: bhūḥsthaiḥ khasthair diviṣṭhaiś ca bhūtair uccāvacair api gaṅgā vigāhyā satatam etat kāryatamaṃ satām
english: By beings high and low — those that dwell on earth, those in the air, and those in heaven — the Gaṅgā is ever to be entered; this is the foremost duty of the good.

sanskrit: triṣu lokeṣu puṇyatvād gaṅgāyāḥ prathitaṃ yaśaḥ yat putrān sagarasyaiṣā bhasmākhyān anayad divam
english: Throughout the three worlds the fame of the Gaṅgā is renowned for her holiness, in that she led the sons of Sagara, reduced to ashes, up to heaven.

sanskrit: vāyvīritābhiḥ sumahāsvanābhir; drutābhir atyarthasamucchritābhiḥ gaṅgormibhir bhānumatībhir iddhaḥ; sahasraraśmipratimo vibhāti
english: Kindled by the gleaming waves of the Gaṅgā — driven by the wind, swift, mightily resounding, and reared up exceedingly high — he shines like the thousand-rayed sun.

sanskrit: payasvinīṃ ghṛtinīm atyudārāṃ; samṛddhinīṃ veginīṃ durvigāhyām gaṅgāṃ gatvā yaiḥ śarīraṃ visṛṣṭaṃ; gatā dhīrās te vibudhaiḥ samatvam
english: Those steadfast ones who, having gone to the Gaṅgā — rich in waters, rich in butter, exceedingly bountiful, abounding, swift, and hard to ford — have given up their bodies there, have attained equality with the gods.

sanskrit: andhāñ jaḍān dravyahīnāṃś ca gaṅgā; yaśasvinī bṛhatī viśvarūpā devaiḥ sendrair munibhir mānavaiś ca; niṣevitā sarvakāmair yunakti
english: The glorious, mighty, all-formed Gaṅgā, served by the gods with Indra, by sages, and by men, joins the blind, the dull, and the destitute to every desire fulfilled.

sanskrit: ūrjāvatīṃ madhumatīṃ mahāpuṇyāṃ trivartmagām trilokagoptrīṃ ye gaṅgāṃ saṃśritās te divaṃ gatāḥ
english: Those who have taken refuge in the Gaṅgā — full of vigor, full of sweetness, most holy, flowing along three courses, the guardian of the three worlds — have gone to heaven.

sanskrit: yo vatsyati drakṣyati vāpi martyas; tasmai prayacchanti sukhāni devāḥ tadbhāvitāḥ sparśane darśane yas; tasmai devā gatim iṣṭāṃ diśanti
english: To the mortal who shall dwell beside her or even behold her, the gods grant joys; and to him whose heart is fixed upon her touch and sight, the gods appoint the goal he desires.

sanskrit: dakṣāṃ pṛthvīṃ bṛhatīṃ viprakṛṣṭāṃ; śivām ṛtāṃ surasāṃ suprasannām vibhāvarīṃ sarvabhūtapratiṣṭhāṃ; gaṅgāṃ gatā ye tridivaṃ gatās te
english: Those who have gone to the Gaṅgā — skillful, broad, mighty, far-extending, auspicious, true, sweet-watered, most serene, radiant, and the foundation of all beings — have gone to the third heaven.

sanskrit: khyātir yasyāḥ khaṃ divaṃ gāṃ ca nityaṃ; purā diśo vidiśaś cāvatasthe tasyā jalaṃ sevya saridvarāyā; martyāḥ sarve kṛtakṛtyā bhavanti
english: She whose renown of old stood firm forever throughout the sky, heaven, and earth, and through the quarters and the intermediate quarters — by resorting to the water of that best of rivers, all mortals attain their every purpose.

sanskrit: iyaṃ gaṅgeti niyataṃ pratiṣṭhā; guhasya rukmasya ca garbhayoṣā prātas trimārgā ghṛtavahā vipāpmā; gaṅgāvatīrṇā viyato viśvatoyā
english: 'This is the Gaṅgā' — she is the steadfast support, the bearer in her womb of Guha and of the golden one; at dawn she runs along three paths, carrying butter, free of all sin, descended from the firmament, her waters poured forth on every side.

sanskrit: sutāvanīdhrasya harasya bhāryā; divo bhuvaś cāpi kakṣyānurūpā bhavyā pṛthivyā bhāvinī bhāti rājan; gaṅgā lokānāṃ puṇyadā vai trayāṇām
english: The consort of Hara, who bears the mountains, befitting the girdle alike of heaven and of earth, gracious, the destiny of the earth — she shines, O king: the Gaṅgā, bestower of merit upon the three worlds.

sanskrit: madhupravāhā ghṛtarāgoddhṛtābhir; mahormibhiḥ śobhitā brāhmaṇaiś ca divaś cyutā śirasāttā bhavena; gaṅgāvanīdhrās tridivasya mālā
english: Her stream is sweet as honey, adorned by great waves uplifted with the hue of butter and by brāhmaṇas as well; fallen from heaven and borne upon Bhava's head, the Gaṅgā, upholder of the earth, is the garland of the third heaven.

sanskrit: yonir variṣṭhā virajā vitanvī; śuṣmā irā vārivahā yaśodā viśvāvatī cākṛtir iṣṭir iddhā; gaṅgokṣitānāṃ bhuvanasya panthāḥ
english: The most excellent womb, stainless, far-spreading, mighty, the nourishing draught, the bearer of waters, the giver of fame, all-containing, very form itself, the sacrifice, kindled — the Gaṅgā is the path of the world for those whom she has sprinkled.

sanskrit: kṣāntyā mahyā gopane dhāraṇe ca; dīptyā kṛśānos tapanasya caiva tulyā gaṅgā saṃmatā brāhmaṇānāṃ; guhasya brahmaṇyatayā ca nityam
english: In forbearance the equal of the earth, in protecting and upholding, and in radiance the equal of fire and of the sun, the Gaṅgā is ever honored by the brāhmaṇas and by Guha's devotion to the brahman.

sanskrit: ṛṣiṣṭutāṃ viṣṇupadīṃ purāṇīṃ; supuṇyatoyāṃ manasāpi loke sarvātmanā jāhnavīṃ ye prapannās; te brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ saṃprayātāḥ
english: Those who in this world have taken refuge with their whole being — even in mind — in the Jāhnavī, praised by sages, sprung from Viṣṇu's foot, ancient, of most holy waters, have gone forth to the abode of Brahmā.

sanskrit: lokān imān nayati yā jananīva putrān; sarvātmanā sarvaguṇopapannā svasthānam iṣṭam iha brāhmam abhīpsamānair; gaṅgā sadaivātmavaśair upāsyā
english: She who leads these worlds onward as a mother leads her sons, endowed in her whole being with every excellence — the Gaṅgā is ever to be honored by the self-controlled who here seek their own desired and holy station, the abode of Brahmā.

sanskrit: usrāṃ juṣṭāṃ miṣatīṃ viśvatoyām; irāṃ vajrīṃ revatīṃ bhūdharāṇām śiṣṭāśrayām amṛtāṃ brahmakāntāṃ; gaṅgāṃ śrayed ātmavān siddhikāmaḥ
english: The self-controlled man who longs for perfection should take refuge in the Gaṅgā — radiant, beloved, ever-watchful, watered on every side, the nourishing draught, armed with the thunderbolt, abounding, the refuge of the mountains, the refuge of the wise, immortal, beloved of Brahmā.

sanskrit: prasādya devān savibhūn samastān; bhagīrathas tapasogreṇa gaṅgām gām ānayat tām abhigamya śaśvan; pumān bhayaṃ neha nāmutra vidyāt
english: Bhagīratha, having propitiated all the gods together with their lords, by fierce austerity brought the Gaṅgā down to earth; and the man who resorts to her unceasingly knows no fear, neither here nor hereafter.

sanskrit: udāhṛtaḥ sarvathā te guṇānāṃ; mayaikadeśaḥ prasamīkṣya buddhyā śaktir na me kā cid ihāsti vaktuṃ; guṇān sarvān parimātuṃ tathaiva
english: Of her virtues I have, having pondered with my understanding, set forth before you but a single portion in every way; I have no power here to tell, or likewise to measure out, all her virtues.

sanskrit: meroḥ samudrasya ca sarvaratnaiḥ; saṃkhyopalānām udakasya vāpi vaktuṃ śakyaṃ neha gaṅgājalānāṃ; guṇākhyānaṃ parimātuṃ tathaiva
english: The whole hoard of jewels of Meru and the ocean, the number of the pebbles, or even of the drops of water, might be told — but here the recital of the virtues of the Gaṅgā's waters can neither be told nor measured out.

sanskrit: tasmād imān parayā śraddhayoktān; guṇān sarvāñ jāhnavījāṃs tathaiva bhajed vācā manasā karmaṇā ca; bhaktyā yuktaḥ parayā śraddadhānaḥ
english: Therefore let a man, joined with supreme devotion and possessed of the highest faith, honor by speech, by mind, and by deed all these virtues of the Jāhnavī, which I have spoken with supreme faith.

sanskrit: lokān imāṃs trīn yaśasā vitatya; siddhiṃ prāpya mahatīṃ tāṃ durāpām gaṅgākṛtān acireṇaiva lokān; yatheṣṭam iṣṭān vicariṣyasi tvam
english: Spreading your fame across these three worlds, and winning that great and hard-won perfection, you shall ere long roam at will through the desired worlds that the Gaṅgā bestows.

sanskrit: tava mama ca guṇair mahānubhāvā; juṣatu matiṃ satataṃ svadharmayuktaiḥ abhigatajanavatsalā hi gaṅgā; bhajati yunakti sukhaiś ca bhaktimantam
english: May the mind of you and of me, exalted in spirit, ever delight in the virtues that belong to our own dharma; for the Gaṅgā, tender toward those who come to her, cherishes the devout one and joins him to every joy.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca iti paramamatir guṇān anekāñ; śilarataye tripathānuyogarūpān bahuvidham anuśāsya tathyarūpān; gaganatalaṃ dyutimān viveśa siddhaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having thus in manifold ways instructed Śilaratin in the many true virtues that pertain to the discourse on the threefold-pathed river, that radiant siddha of supreme wisdom entered the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: śilavṛttis tu siddhasya vākyaiḥ saṃbodhitas tadā gaṅgām upāsya vidhivat siddhiṃ prāptaḥ sudurlabhām
english: And Śilavṛtti, then enlightened by the words of the siddha, having honored the Gaṅgā according to the rule, attained that perfection most hard to win.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam api kaunteya bhaktyā paramayā yutaḥ gaṅgām abhyehi satataṃ prāpsyase siddhim uttamām
english: Therefore you too, son of Kuntī, joined with supreme devotion, resort unceasingly to the Gaṅgā, and you shall attain the highest perfection.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvetihāsaṃ bhīṣmoktaṃ gaṅgāyāḥ stavasaṃyutam yudhiṣṭhiraḥ parāṃ prītim agacchad bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this tale told by Bhīṣma, joined with the praise of the Gaṅgā, Yudhiṣṭhira together with his brothers attained the highest joy.

sanskrit: itihāsam imaṃ puṇyaṃ śṛṇuyād yaḥ paṭheta vā gaṅgāyāḥ stavasaṃyuktaṃ sa mucyet sarvakilbiṣaiḥ
english: Whoever should hear or recite this holy tale, joined with the praise of the Gaṅgā, would be released from all his sins.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca prajñāśrutābhyāṃ vṛttena śīlena ca yathā bhavān guṇaiḥ samuditaḥ sarvair vayasā ca samanvitaḥ tasmād bhavantaṃ pṛcchāmi dharmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Since you, O best of the upholders of dharma, are endowed with wisdom and learning, with conduct and character, with all the virtues, and with the fullness of years, therefore I ask you concerning dharma.

sanskrit: kṣatriyo yadi vā vaiśyaḥ śūdro vā rājasattama brāhmaṇyaṃ prāpnuyāt kena tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: By what means, O best of kings, might a kṣatriya, or a vaiśya, or a śūdra attain brāhmaṇahood? This you ought to explain to me.

sanskrit: tapasā vā sumahatā karmaṇā vā śrutena vā brāhmaṇyam atha ced icchet tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: If one should desire brāhmaṇahood, whether by very great austerity, or by ritual works, or by sacred learning — tell me this, grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca brāhmaṇyaṃ tāta duṣprāpaṃ varṇaiḥ kṣatrādibhis tribhiḥ paraṃ hi sarvabhūtānāṃ sthānam etad yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: Brāhmaṇahood, dear son, is hard for the three orders headed by the kṣatriyas to attain; for this, Yudhiṣṭhira, is the highest station of all beings.

sanskrit: bahvīs tu saṃsaran yonīr jāyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ paryāye tāta kasmiṃś cid brāhmaṇo nāma jāyate
english: Passing through many wombs, being born again and again, only in some turn of the cycle, dear son, is one born as a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam mataṅgasya ca saṃvādaṃ gardabhyāś ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this point too they tell this ancient tale, Yudhiṣṭhira: the dialogue of Mataṅga and the she-ass.

sanskrit: dvijāteḥ kasya cit tāta tulyavarṇaḥ sutaḥ prabhuḥ mataṅgo nāma nāmnābhūt sarvaiḥ samudito guṇaiḥ
english: There was, dear son, a mighty son of a certain twice-born man, of like color to his father, Mataṅga by name, endowed with every virtue.

sanskrit: sa yajñakāraḥ kaunteya pitrā sṛṣṭaḥ paraṃtapa prāyād gardabhayuktena rathenehāśugāminā
english: That performer of sacrifice, O son of Kuntī, scorcher of foes, sent forth by his father, set out upon a swift-going chariot yoked with asses.

sanskrit: sa bālaṃ gardabhaṃ rājan vahantaṃ mātur antike niravidhyat pratodena nāsikāyāṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: He, O king, with his goad pierced again and again upon the nose a young ass that was drawing the chariot beside its mother.

sanskrit: taṃ tu tīvravraṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā gardabhī putragṛddhinī uvāca mā śucaḥ putra caṇḍālas tvādhitiṣṭhati
english: But the she-ass, yearning for her offspring, seeing him grievously wounded, said: 'Grieve not, my child; it is a caṇḍāla who sits over you.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇe dāruṇaṃ nāsti maitro brāhmaṇa ucyate ācāryaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ śāstā kiṃ prahariṣyati
english: 'In a brāhmaṇa there is no cruelty; a brāhmaṇa is called the friend of all. He is the teacher and chastiser of all beings — why would he strike?'

sanskrit: ayaṃ tu pāpaprakṛtir bāle na kurute dayām svayoniṃ mānayaty eṣa bhāvo bhāvaṃ nigacchati
english: 'But this one, of evil nature, shows no mercy to a young creature; he does but honor his own origin — a nature passes on to its like.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā mataṅgas tu dāruṇaṃ rāsabhīvacaḥ avatīrya rathāt tūrṇaṃ rāsabhīṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Hearing this harsh speech of the she-ass, Mataṅga quickly stepped down from the chariot and answered her.

sanskrit: brūhi rāsabhi kalyāṇi mātā me yena dūṣitā kathaṃ māṃ vetsi caṇḍālaṃ kṣipraṃ rāsabhi śaṃsa me
english: 'Tell me, gracious she-ass, by whom was my mother defiled? How do you know me to be a caṇḍāla? Quickly, she-ass, declare it to me.'

sanskrit: kena jāto 'smi caṇḍālo brāhmaṇyaṃ yena me 'naśat tattvenaitan mahāprājñe brūhi sarvam aśeṣataḥ
english: 'By whom was I born a caṇḍāla, so that my brāhmaṇahood is lost to me? Tell me this truly, O most wise one, all of it without reserve.'

sanskrit: gardabhy uvāca brāhmaṇyāṃ vṛṣalena tvaṃ mattāyāṃ nāpitena ha jātas tvam asi caṇḍālo brāhmaṇyaṃ tena te 'naśat
english: The she-ass said: 'You were begotten by a śūdra, a barber, upon a brāhmaṇa woman maddened with drink; therefore you are a caṇḍāla, and therefore your brāhmaṇahood is lost.'

sanskrit: evam ukto mataṅgas tu pratyupāyād gṛhaṃ prati tam āgatam abhiprekṣya pitā vākyam athābravīt
english: Thus addressed, Mataṅga turned back homeward; and seeing him return, his father then spoke these words.

sanskrit: mayā tvaṃ yajñasaṃsiddhau niyukto gurukarmaṇi kasmāt pratinivṛtto 'si kaccin na kuśalaṃ tava
english: 'By me you were appointed to the weighty task of the completion of the sacrifice; why have you turned back? Is it that all is not well with you?'

sanskrit: mataṅga uvāca ayonir agryayonir vā yaḥ syāt sa kuśalī bhavet kuśalaṃ tu kutas tasya yasyeyaṃ jananī pitaḥ
english: Mataṅga said: 'He may be well whose birth is from no womb, or from the highest womb; but whence can there be well-being for him whose mother is such as this, O father?'
